title: Completed proper/open realization and its projection normalization without a Tor bound
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $\ell$ a prime invertible in $k$, and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,\overline X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] and $X\xrightarrow j\overline X\xrightarrow pY$ a compactification of $f=pj$, with $j$ quasi-compact open and $p$ proper [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. On their small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $R_T=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use ordinary unbounded module-sheaf derived categories, ordinary completed-ring direct image $Rp_{*,R}$, exact localized extension by zero $j_!$, and finite analogues $Rp_{*,n},j_{!,n}$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization].

For $K\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] put $K_n=K\otimes^L_{R_X}(A_n)_X$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]. The canonical completion map, strict open-tensor comparison, and direct-image/derived-limit comparison specify a natural isomorphism
$$d_c(K):Rp_{*,R}j_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n Rp_{*,n}j_{!,n}K_n=Rf_!^cK.$$
The tower and its quotient transitions on the right are exactly those of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], and $R\varprojlim$ is the functor on strict towers [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Both $j_!K$ and $Rp_{*,R}j_!K$ are derived-complete constructible objects. The reduction of $d_c$ identifies the canonical comparison of $Rf_!^c$ with the ordered composite of the perfect-coefficient projection map for $p$ and the open-tensor map for $j$.

For any $L\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ for which all displayed tensor expressions belong to these categories, $d_c$ intertwines the compact-support projection map formed by the completed $p^*\dashv Rp_*$ counit and open tensor with the realized strict-tower map of the finite counit-defined projection maps. Here completed pullback and tensor are [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], and projection maps are [def-exchange-projection]. This is equality of the specified derived morphisms, including the quotient transitions before total limit. No uniform finite Tor-amplitude assumption on $K$ is imposed.

source.place: Paragraph 2: applying ordinary direct-image reduction to the proper factor and extension by zero; original split steps 5-6, with the projection normalization from step 10. Ringed limit ingredient: Stacks Tag 0A07 (sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim).

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_E$ and $H=j_!K$. The DVR theorem makes $A$ Noetherian: it is a principal ideal domain, so every ideal has one generator. The standard-quotient theorem gives finite sets $A_n$ and perfect two-term resolutions $[A\xrightarrow{t^n}A]$. Thus $(A,(t))$ satisfies the adic hypotheses in the direct-image and perfect-projection lemmas (the finite residue field has characteristic $\ell$, so $A/(t)$ is additive torsion). A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and itself; its spectrum is a one-point affine scheme. Finite type over this Noetherian base makes $X,\overline X,Y$ Noetherian. The compactification already supplies the quasi-compact open $j$; no existence of a new compactification is used.

source.place: paragraph 2, two-term perfect quotient; verification of the hypotheses of the cited adic and open lemmas

proof.text: Use the specified strict open reduction $r_j(K)$, not a separately chosen family of levelwise isomorphisms. It gives $H_n\cong j_{!,n}K_n$, respects quotient transitions and reduction augmentations, and says that $H$ is derived complete with its actual completion unit. If all $K_n$ have cohomology in $[a,b]$, the finite open-extension theorem gives constructibility of $j_{!,n}K_n$ and the same interval $[a,b]$. Consequently $H\in D^b_c(\overline X,\mathcal O_E)$ by the definition of that category. This uses uniform cohomological boundedness of the reductions, without a Tor bound.

source.place: Lemmas 6.1.13 and 6.5.8; strict open reduction is the cited agent refinement of Stacks 0GL1

proof.text:
Let $\eta_H:H\to R\lim\operatorname{Res}_nH_n$ be this completion unit. Apply the strict direct-image/limit comparison to $p$. Restriction of coefficients identifies $Rp_{*,R}\operatorname{Res}_n$ with $\operatorname{Res}_nRp_{*,n}$ as derived strict-diagram functors. Hence the composite
$$a_H:Rp_{*,R}H\xrightarrow{Rp_{*,R}\eta_H}Rp_{*,R}R\lim\operatorname{Res}_nH_n\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim\operatorname{Res}_nRp_{*,n}H_n$$
is a natural isomorphism. It is normalized so that its $n$-th projection is $Rp_{*,R}$ of the reduction augmentation, followed by coefficient restriction. The direct-image theorem also gives derived completeness of $Rp_{*,R}H$. In the coefficient-restriction lemma its auxiliary prime $p_0\ne\ell$ can be chosen arbitrarily; that lemma imposes no characteristic condition on the schemes.

source.place: Tag 0A07, lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim, first proof on the sequence topoi; coefficient restriction also uses Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition

proof.text: Set $N_n=\operatorname{Res}_nRp_{*,n}H_n$ and $M_n=\operatorname{Res}_nRp_{*,n}j_{!,n}K_n$. Applying proper image to the strict open comparison defines $\beta_n:N_n\xrightarrow{\sim}M_n$. The proper-image tower lemma gives $\beta_n t^N_n=t^M_n\beta_{n+1}$ with $t^M_n$ precisely the compact-support restriction-of-scalars transition. These maps come from $r_j(K)$ and derived direct image on the coefficient diagram, so this is the specified strict-diagram comparison of Step 3. Define $d_c(K)=R\lim(\beta_\bullet)\circ a_H$. Functoriality of total derived limit makes this an isomorphism. The definition of integral compact support identifies its target and all the transitions with $Rf_!^cK$.

source.place: paragraph 2, applying direct-image reduction to the proper factor and extension by zero; explicit quotient transitions

proof.text: The integral direct-image constructibility theorem applies to $p$ and $H$ from Step 2. Its integral direct image is defined as the right-hand tower in $a_H$, and Step 3 identifies this with ordinary $Rp_{*,R}H$. Therefore $Rp_{*,R}j_!K$ lies in $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, with the theorem's uniform cohomological bound. This use of constructibility concerns all bounded constructible finite reductions; it does not replace that category by the finite-Tor constructible category.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2; the cited DAG theorem states the bounded finite-stalk version needed here

proof.text:
For every $n$, perfect-coefficient projection gives the specified isomorphism $\pi_{p,H,A_n}:(Rp_{*,R}H)_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_{*,n}H_n$ after coefficient restriction. Its composite with $Rp_{*,n}(r_j(K)_n)$ is the ordered comparison
$$(Rp_{*,R}j_!K)_n\xrightarrow{\pi_{p,H,A_n}}Rp_{*,n}(j_!K)_n\xrightarrow{Rp_{*,n}(r_j(K)_n)}Rp_{*,n}j_{!,n}K_n.$$
The direct-image/limit theorem identifies the completion map with this projection-formula comparison on the entire augmented quotient diagram. The reduction/limit adjunction identifies its evaluated map with the scalar-extension adjoint of the actual limit projection. Thus this is exactly the reduction comparison induced by $d_c$, including the quotient transitions, rather than just an isomorphism between its source and target.

source.place: paragraph 2, canonical perfect-coefficient projection comparison; Stacks sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0943, section-projection-formula

proof.text: For the projection assertion, write $U_T$ for restriction from $R_T$-modules to constant-$A$ modules, only on derived-complete objects. The constant/completion theorem makes $U_T$ an equivalence there and identifies reductions, total limits and completion units. Both $U_T(M\widehat\otimes N)$ and the constant-coefficient completed tensor of $U_TM,U_TN$ are the total limit of the same strict system $M_n\otimes^L_{A_n}N_n$: use the theorem's change-of-rings isomorphisms and the strict tensor reduction comparison. The maps are tensor reassociation, so they respect associators and units. The theorem's pullback reduction comparison similarly identifies completed pullbacks by their defining strict limit, naturally in the whole input system. Completed-operation substitution fixes these identifications on nested expressions and their structural maps. This is a construction of comparisons by strict system maps, without using faithfulness of individual reductions.

source.place: Tag 099I, lemma-restriction-derived-complete-equivalence, with sites-modules.tex Tag 093M, lemma-completion-flat; tensor and pullback reassociation for the common finite quotients

proof.text:
These identifications preserve the actual completed adjunction. Indeed let $Q_R=Lp_R^*$, $Q_A=p^{-1}$, and $\kappa:U_YRp_{*,R}\cong Rp_{*,A}U_{\overline X}$. The coefficient-restriction counit theorem gives
$$U_{\overline X}(\varepsilon_R)\,\tau_{Rp_{*,R}H}=\varepsilon_A\,Q_A(\kappa_H),$$
where $\tau$ is induced by $x\mapsto1\otimes x$. The common-quotient pullback comparison of Step 7 is the completion of this same $\tau$. The reflector adjunction formula says that the completed counit precomposed with the completion unit equals the ordinary counit. Since precomposition with that unit is bijective for maps into complete $H$, the displayed ordinary counit identity implies the completed counit identity under Step 7's equivalences. Here the completion reflector and its unit over $R_T$ are the Koszul reflector, identified with quotient-tower completion by the constant/completion theorem. Thus the constant completed adjunction and completed-ring adjunction have the same specified counits under these comparisons.

source.place: Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint, and Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; completing the canonical counit through the reflector

proof.text: Apply completed projection coherence with constant ring $A$, ideal $(t)$, proper map $p$, and complete inputs $U_{\overline X}H,U_YL$. Its hypotheses are Step 1's Noetherian and perfect-quotient facts; no Tor condition is present. It identifies the constant completed counit-defined projection with the total limit of the actual finite projection mates on the ringed coefficient diagram, including transitions. Steps 7-8 identify its tensor comparison, pullback comparison, direct image and counit with those of the completed-ring projection. Consequently full faithfulness of $U_Y$ on complete objects gives the same equality for that specified completed-ring projection. This uses an equality of total-limit morphisms supplied by the coherence theorem, not a claim that equal finite evaluations imply equal integral morphisms.

source.place: Tags 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map, 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, and 0A07, lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim; agent-derived completion coherence is the cited statement

proof.text: Finally realize the strict open-tensor comparison on the coefficient diagram. Open reduction identifies realized extension by zero with ordinary $j_!$ and fixes its adjunction unit; completed-operation substitution identifies the tensor and pullback vertices, including $j^*p^*\cong f^*$. Its open restriction is the identity by the normalization of open tensor. The completed open-tensor map has the same restriction; both its source and target are open extensions (the strict open-tensor isomorphism and the open realization provide this identification). Full faithfulness of $j_!$ therefore identifies these specified maps. Compose this equality after the proper projection equality of Step 9 and use $d_c$ at both compact-support arguments. By the defining ordered formula for $\operatorname{PF}^c$, the result is precisely the asserted projection square. All maps were constructed on the strict coefficient diagrams before total limit. The assumed domain condition on $L$ supplies every bounded constructible vertex used here. For $K=0$, $X=\varnothing$, or an empty open all maps are the zero-object identifications; for identity $j$ and identity $p$ the open unit and proper counit normalizations give the respective identity comparisons.
